question:
A 32-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Department after 3 consecutive days of diarrhea, fatigue and weakness. His stool has been soft and mucoid, with no blood stains. The patient just came back from a volunteer mission in Guatemala, where he remained asymptomatic. His personal medical history is unremarkable. Today his blood pressure is 98/60 mm Hg, pulse is 110/min, respiratory rate is 19/min, and his body temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F). On physical exam, he has sunken eyes, dry mucosa, mild diffuse abdominal tenderness, and hyperactive bowel sounds. Initial laboratory tests are shown below:
Serum creatinine (SCr) 1.8 mg/dL
Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 50 mg/dL
Serum sodium 132 mEq/L
Serum potassium 3.5 mEq/L
Serum chloride 102 mEq/L
Which of the following phenomena would you expect in this patient?

options.opa: High urine osmolality, high fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa+), high urine Na+
options.opb: High urine osmolality, low FeNa+, low urine Na+
options.opc: Low urine osmolality, high FeNa+, high urine Na+
options.opd: Low urine osmolality, low FeNa+, high urine Na+
options.ope: Low urine osmolality, high FeNa+, low urine Na+

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Diarrhea" -> "Dehydration" -> "Decreased blood volume" -> "Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system" -> "Increased reabsorption of sodium and water in the kidneys" -> "Low urine osmolality, low FeNa+, high urine Na+" -> 80% CHAIN: "Dehydration" -> "Hypovolemia" -> "Decreased renal perfusion" -> "Activation of the sympathetic nervous system" -> "Increased renin release" -> "Increased aldosterone secretion" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption in the kidneys" -> "Low urine osmolality, low FeNa+, high urine Na+" -> 85% CHAIN: "Dehydration" -> "Hypovolemia" -> "Decreased renal perfusion" -> "Increased renin release" -> "Increased aldosterone secretion" -> "Increased sodium reabsorption in the kidneys" -> "Low urine osmolality, high FeNa+, high urine Na+" -> 80%
analysis: The patient is presenting with signs and symptoms of dehydration and prerenal azotemia, likely due to acute gastroenteritis. The elevated BUN and creatinine with a low urine output suggest decreased renal perfusion leading to decreased glomerular filtration rate. This would result in a low urine osmolality, high FeNa+, and high urine Na+.
